prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a low-speed head-on collision claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1500; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a low-speed head-on collision reported by the insured. Initial contact made with the claimant. Claimant reports neck and lower back discomfort and has retained counsel, who has requested that all communication be directed through their office. Vehicle inspection to be scheduled.

Entry 2: Vehicle inspected at the repair facility. Front bumper cover, radiator support and both headlamp assemblies show damage consistent with a low-speed frontal impact. Photographs uploaded to file. Estimate requested from the body shop and pending review.

Entry 3: Spoke with claimant's attorney's office. Counsel confirms client was treated at urgent care for back strain and has been advised to limit lifting and attend physical therapy. Medical authorization forms requested and sent. Awaiting signed release before records can be obtained.

Entry 4: Received treatment records from the urgent care provider. Diagnosis listed as acute lumbar strain with no fractures or imaging findings of concern. Records reviewed and noted in file. Follow-up request sent to the physical therapy clinic for attendance and progress notes.

Entry 5: Physical therapy notes received showing the claimant is attending sessions as scheduled and reports gradual improvement in range of motion. No surgery or specialist referral indicated at this time. Claim remains open pending final repair estimate, medical billing review, and settlement discussions with counsel.
